value.body: Several state governments own aircraft and helicopters for official travel and emergencies, usually run by a state civil aviation department. They employ licensed aircraft maintenance engineers to keep these aircraft airworthy.

items.label: Licence
items.note: With endorsement on the state's aircraft type

items.label: Experience
items.note: Hours and years are stated in each notice

items.label: DGCA-approved AME training institutes
items.note: Approved under CAR-147 (Basic); counts vary by source and date
items.source: Lok Sabha reply, Ministry of Civil Aviation (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: States advertise through their civil aviation department. Posts generally need a DGCA licence endorsed for the state's aircraft type and prior maintenance experience; selection is by interview. Many posts are on contract.

value.title: At a glance
items: Openings are rare; a state may have only a handful of posts.
These are experienced-engineer posts, not fresher roles.
Work follows official flying schedules, often at short notice.
